hostRules.description: read:packages auth for the private org GitHub Packages NuGet feed (FS.GG.* are not on nuget.org). Lives in this repo's own config — NOT the shared preset — because Renovate does not substitute {{ secrets }} inside presets pulled via extends. Value = org-level Mend App Secret FSGG_PACKAGES_READ_TOKEN.

packageRules.description: #300 — NEVER propose FS.GG.UI.* bumps under samples/. The four out-of-solution sample suites map FS.GG.UI.* exclusively to the machine-local feed (see each samples/*/nuget.config packageSourceMapping), which only a local `dotnet pack` of src/ fills, at src/*/*.fsproj <Version>. Renovate's datasource is nuget.pkg.github.com — a feed these projects are configured never to read — so every version it can see is one they cannot resolve (NU1102). That is PR #233: it proposed the published 0.4.0 against a tree pinned to 0.4.0-preview.1 and merged 4/4 green, because nothing in CI read the files it changed. Both halves of that hole are now closed: the required gate checks the pin mirrors <Version>, and packaged-consumer.yml builds the samples against a feed packed from the commit. This rule stops the bot re-proposing, every cycle, a bump the gate now rejects. The pin moves ONLY with the release: commit that moves src <Version>, never on its own.

Do NOT propose bumps to the DISTRIBUTED build-config files. Directory.Packages.props, Directory.Build.props and .config/dotnet-tools.json are the FS-GG org-shared baseline, synced from FS-GG/.github by scripts/sync-build-config.sh and marked 'DO NOT EDIT in a consumer repo'. Any local edit reds the REQUIRED Build-config drift gate by design, so a Renovate PR touching them — e.g. the FSharp.Core / dotnet baseline — can NEVER merge; it just churns every cycle and burns a review (see closed #790). Those bumps flow through the build-config sync, not here. Repo-owned pins (SkiaSharp, Expecto, the test SDK, etc.) live in Directory.Packages.local.props and stay managed.

Move Expecto and its test-SDK adapter as one unit — they must stay version-compatible, so they bump together in a single PR rather than as two that momentarily conflict. This is what makes the Expecto 11 move land as one coherent PR now that the cap is gone (#845). The cap this rule used to wait on ('Expecto is capped to the 10.x line…, ACTION WHEN YoloDev.Expecto.TestSdk ships a release supporting Expecto >= 11: delete this allowedVersions cap') was RETIRED by its own stated trigger: adapter 0.16.0 depends on Expecto 10.2.3 as a MINIMUM with no upper bound (verified against the nuspec on api.nuget.org, not inferred from the version number), and this repo has been on 0.16.0 for some time — so the adapter had stopped constraining Expecto and the cap was the only thing holding it at 10.x. What still needs saying is the part the cap did NOT: the adapter's own latest, 1.0.0, is a DOWNGRADE — it depends on Expecto [9.0.0, 10.0.0), a HIGHER number on an OLDER lineage, and 0.16.0 in the middle is the only version that admits Expecto 11. Renovate reads versions, not lineages. That fact is now enforced for every repo by `allowedVersions: <1.0.0` on YoloDev.Expecto.TestSdk in the SHARED preset (FS-GG/.github default.json, .github#850) rather than six times over, which is what makes deleting the cap here safe — deleting it while the adapter was uncapped would have let Renovate propose 1.0.0 and force Expecto back to 9.x (NU1608, warning-as-error).
